prompt.en: Write the final line. Why is a seed alive when a flame is not?

text.en: A flame and a seed are made of the same few atoms, held by the same grips, and run the same reaction: fuel and oxygen, downhill. The flame runs it as a short circuit: one drop, all heat, no wall, nothing kept. The seed runs it inside a wall, in about thirty small steps, and catches about a third of the fall as coins. It spends the coins keeping its inside different from the outside, building its own machines from recipes on a tape, reading the tape with a machine made of tape, sensing and signalling, and copying the tape with small errors, so that its kind changes over generations. The seed is a loop: the tape builds the machines, the machines catch energy, the energy keeps the wall and copies the tape. The boiled seed has every part and the loop is broken: its machines are unfolded and it sits at the valley floor. The flame never had a loop. The seed is alive because the loop is closed. That is not a line in the Ledger. It is all of them, joined.
